title: Infinitesimal divisor-to-Picard map and its kernel
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective], let $P\in C(k)$, and fix a Jacobian $(J,\varphi)$ [def-sc-jacobian]. For an integer $r\geq0$, let $H_r$ represent the effective divisors of degree $r$ [thm-pc-hilb-curves], and let $a_r:H_r\to J$ be the morphism sending $D$ to $[\mathcal O_C(D-rP)]$, constructed from [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism] and tensoring with $\mathcal O_C(-rP)$ [def-sc-divisor]. For every effective divisor $D$ of degree $r$, the tangent space [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] $T_{H_r/k,D}$ identifies with $H^0(C,\mathcal O_D(D))$, where $\mathcal O_D(D):=\mathcal O_C(D)/\mathcal O_C$. Under the identification $T_{J/k,0}\simeq H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ obtained from the Picard tangent space [lem-sc-pic-tangent-space] through $\varphi$, followed by translation from $a_r(D)$ to $0$, the differential of $a_r$ is the connecting map of $0\to\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal O_C(D)\to\mathcal O_D(D)\to0$, up to the sign convention for connecting maps. In particular the sequence of $k$-vector spaces
$$0\longrightarrow k\longrightarrow H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))\longrightarrow T_{H_r/k,D}\xrightarrow{\mathrm da_r}T_{J/k,a_r(D)}$$
is exact, with cohomology in the sense of [pqf-def-cohomology], and $\dim_k\ker(\mathrm da_r)_D=h^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))-1$.

source.place: Chapter III Theorem 5.1(b), pp.101–103, especially the kernel-dimension computation at the end of p.103; the boundary-map formulation is the first-order local-equation refinement of that computation (explained in report.md), with Picard tangent space from Proposition 2.1, pp.90–91.

proof.text: First [lem-pc-projective-proper] makes $C$ proper. By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] it is Noetherian and integral; with the given point $P$, [prop-pc-xk-integral] gives geometric integrality, so the hypotheses of the Hilbert and Picard statements are satisfied (an algebraically closed field is separably closed). A degree-$r$ effective divisor is an effective Cartier divisor by [thm-pc-hilb-curves]. Use [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc] to identify its valuation-defined module with the dual of its Cartier ideal. Thus the local rational functions, the Hilbert universal divisor line bundle, and the Picard class in this proof refer to the same invertible module.

source.place: Tag 0B9I proposition-hilb-d and Tag 0BA0 lemma-picard-pieces, with the existing divisor-convention comparison.

proof.text: Put $A=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and $\mathcal I=\mathcal O_C(-D)$. By [lem-sc-divisor-module-local], choose affine opens $U_i$ where $\mathcal I=(f_i)$ and $\mathcal O_C(D)=f_i^{-1}\mathcal O_{U_i}$, with $f_i$ a non-zero-divisor. By the representing Hilbert functor and the dual-number definition of tangent vectors, a tangent vector at $D$ is a finite locally free degree-$r$ closed subscheme of $C_A$ reducing to $D$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-embedded-dual-number-graphs]: these are exactly maps $h:\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_C/\mathcal I$. Locally send $h$ to $h(f_i)/f_i$ modulo $\mathcal O_C$. This gives a sheaf isomorphism $\mathcal H om(\mathcal I,\mathcal O_C/\mathcal I)\simeq\mathcal O_C(D)/\mathcal O_C$: if $f_j=u_{ij}f_i$, linearity gives $h(f_j)=u_{ij}h(f_i)$, so the fractions agree; locally its inverse sends $g_i/f_i$ to the map $f_i\mapsto g_i\bmod f_i$. Global sections give the asserted tangent identification. The scalar and two-parameter formulas in the graph lemma agree with the tangent operations, so it is $k$-linear, including $D=0$.

source.place: Chapter III Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 5.1(b), pp.90–91 and 101–103; agent local-equation refinement of the boundary-map assertion.

proof.text: For $s\in H^0(C,\mathcal O_D(D))$, refine $\{U_i\}$ (the restricted $f_i$ remain local equations) so that each $s|_{U_i}$ lifts, which is possible because $\mathcal O_C(D)\to\mathcal O_D(D)$ is an epimorphism of sheaves, and choose representatives $q_i=g_i/f_i\in\mathcal O_C(D)(U_i)$. Its graph ideal is generated locally by $F_i=f_i+\epsilon g_i$: indeed $af_i+\epsilon b$ belongs to the graph iff $b-ag_i$ is divisible by $f_i$. This generator is a non-zero-divisor, since $F_i(a+\epsilon b)=0$ first gives $f_i a=0$, then $f_i b=0$. On overlaps $q_j-q_i\in\mathcal O_C$, and $F_j=u_{ij}(1+\epsilon(q_j-q_i))F_i$. Thus the transition ratios for $\mathcal O(D_A)$ relative to $p^*\mathcal O(D)$ are $1+\epsilon(q_j-q_i)$ (or their inverses if frames are ordered oppositely), by the dual-ideal definition of the divisor line bundle. The Hilbert-to-Picard morphism on $A$-points is the class of this very divisor line bundle, not merely its closed-fibre class: if $x:\operatorname{Spec}A\to H_r$ is the tangent vector, then $\gamma_r\circ x$ corresponds by Yoneda to the pullback of $[\mathcal O(D_r)]$, the pullback of the universal subscheme is $D_A$ by the definition of the representing isomorphism, and the pullback of a local generator of the universal ideal generates the ideal of $D_A$, hence is a unit multiple of the non-zero-divisor $F_i$; so the pulled-back invertible ideal maps isomorphically onto $\mathcal I_{D_A}$, and dualizing gives $\mathcal O(D_A)$. Translation by $-a_r(D)$ tensors with $p^*\mathcal O_C(-D+rP)$; the fixed $-rP$ twist cancels, leaving $\mathcal O(D_A)\otimes p^*\mathcal O(-D)$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-thickening-picard-cocycle] and the representing group isomorphism of [def-sc-jacobian]: the translated differential corresponds to the image of the additive cocycle $(q_j-q_i)$ in $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, up to the single sign convention just specified.

source.place: Chapter III Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 5.1(b), pp.90–91 and 101–103; agent local-equation refinement of the boundary-map assertion.

proof.text: The local lifts $q_i$ are lifts of the same section $s$ of $\mathcal O_D(D)$ for the short exact module-sheaf sequence $0\to\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal O_C(D)\to\mathcal O_D(D)\to0$. The statement of [lem-sc-boundary-cech-compatibility] sends precisely the differences $q_j-q_i$ under the canonical Cech comparison to its connecting class $\delta(s)$. Therefore the differential computed in the preceding step is $\delta$, up to the allowed sign. This proves the map comparison, not just equality of dimensions or kernels.

source.place: Tag 0B8S, lemma-boundary-derivation-over-cup-product, local-lift calculation; sign fixed by the cited node.

proof.text: Let $i:D\hookrightarrow C$. Locally multiplication by $f_i$ identifies $\mathcal O_C(D)/\mathcal O_C$ with $i_*i^*\mathcal O_C(D)$, since $f_i^{-1}\mathcal O/(\mathcal O)\simeq\mathcal O/(f_i)$. Apply [lem-sfb-closed-immersion-cokernel-cohomology] to $0\to\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal O_C(D)\to i_*i^*\mathcal O_C(D)\to0$: its specified boundary gives an exact sequence of $k$-vector spaces starting with $0\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_D(D))\to H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$. By [lem-sc-global-functions] its first nonzero term is $k$ (projective implies proper, and the smooth curve satisfies the lemma's final clause). Substituting Steps 2–4 gives the displayed exact sequence; changing the final map's sign does not change its kernel.

source.place: Chapter III Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 5.1(b), pp.90–91 and 101–103; agent local-equation refinement of the boundary-map assertion.

proof.text: The invertible module $\mathcal O_C(D)$ is coherent on the Noetherian curve: on each trivializing affine its module is free of rank one. Hence [lem-pc-curve-coherent-finiteness] makes $V=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))$ finite dimensional. Step 5 identifies $\ker(\mathrm da_r)_D$ with the image of $V$, whose kernel is the embedded one-dimensional subspace of constants. Choosing a basis of that subspace and extending it to a basis of $V$ gives a basis of the quotient, so $\dim_k\ker(\mathrm da_r)_D=\dim_kV-1=h^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))-1$.
